construct: ATP7B is a hepatocellular copper-transporting ATPase involved in incorporating copper into ceruloplasmin and exporting excess copper into bile. Loss of ATP7B function impairs both processes, causing hepatic copper accumulation and reduced circulating ceruloplasmin.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Adolescent hepatic and neurologic disease with Kayser-Fleischer rings, low ceruloplasmin, and increased urinary copper identifies Wilson disease from ATP7B dysfunction.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: ATP7A is a copper transporter and therefore superficially plausible, but ATP7A dysfunction causes Menkes disease and impaired intestinal/systemic copper delivery; Wilson disease specifically reflects hepatocellular ATP7B failure of biliary excretion and ceruloplasmin loading.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The key combines the two documented hepatocellular ATP7B functions and uniquely explains copper retention with low ceruloplasmin.
